text:
maria: Quick update — SLIM (Sequence Length Inference Microbatcher) is live on canary.
maria: TL;DR: we predict request sequence length early and pre-bucket requests so the packer creates length-homogeneous microbatches instead of waiting for EOS. Results: p50 latency down ~22%, p99 down ~35ms, token cost ~14% lower on generation-heavy traffic.

sanjay: awesome — which models and traffic split?

maria: canary config: 5% production traffic across a shard group; models tested: redwood/4k-q, rw-chat-13b, and a hybrid quantized 7b variant. Also ran synthetic replay with our top-10 prompt templates.

deploy-bot: Canary finished — 1732109900 — all health checks green, canary perf vs baseline: p50 -22.1%, p95 -18.7%, p99 -34.6ms, token-cost -13.9% :white_check_mark:

alex: observability note — measured ~18% GPU utilization efficiency boost on the microbatcher fleet (more even token packing). Biggest wins on short-answer workloads like search/snippets.

jess: did we see any quality regressions? early-bucketing sounds risky for some streaming prompts.

maria: good question. We ran ~1k eval prompts (QA + summarization). Quality deltas were within noise (<0.2% uplift/delta across our metrics). We also added a safety fallback: if per-prompt prefix-score drops by >0.5% on canary, rollout auto-rolls back to `batcher.v1`.

ryan: rollout plan?

maria: Plan: 5% -> 20% (12h) -> 50% (24h) -> 100% (48h) with automated gates. Ops oncall is briefed and we added canary monitors.

ops-bot: ops-bot: Added dashboard panels: `slim-batcher.p99_latency`, `slim-batcher.token_cost_delta`, `slim-batcher.quality_delta`. Auto-alert: 10m burn if p99 > baseline+50ms or quality_delta > 0.5%.

sanjay: PR + config snippet: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/7890
sanjay: ```
microbatcher:
  strategy: slim
  estimator: seqlen-v1
  bucket_count: 8
  max_microbatch_ms: 12
  fallback: batcher.v1
```

maria: tagging @sanjay @alex to own post-rollout smoke tests. Also pushed a shortrun: `tools/bench/replay --prompts top10 --target slim-canary` if you want to reproduce numbers locally.

alex: love it, nice work team :tada: :rocket:

jess: handoff note: update runbooks and make sure support has the FAQ (why some requests get grouped). I'll draft the blurb.

maria: thanks all — will post formal summary + graphs to #eng-runtime tomorrow AM. :thumbsup:
